**Finding submitted: deviation (high severity), confidence 0.83**

**What the document says.** The only licence grant is paragraph 2 (p0002): Kubient grants *Customer* a "limited, royalty-free, non-exclusive, non-transferable, non-assignable, without right of sublicense, **revocable** license" to the Auction Platform.

**Why it fails the fallback.**
- **Affiliates/contractors excluded with no path to add them.** The grant names only "Customer." For an ad-serving platform placing Creative on our websites via Google Ad Manager, our affiliates and the contractors who run that inventory are the actual operational users. Even the fallback requires affiliate coverage on written notice; there is none.
- **Revocable at will.** "Revocable" is unqualified. Paragraph 4(c)(ii) (p0021) already revokes the licence on termination, so the standalone "revocable" adds nothing except discretionary revocation mid-term — squarely the walk-away case.

**What I did not flag.** The assignment clause (p0072) lets either party assign without consent to an affiliate, a purchaser of substantially all assets, or a merger/stock-sale successor. That satisfies the fallback's successor-transfer element, so I carved "non-assignable" back to that clause rather than deleting the transfer restrictions outright — a smaller edit that avoids re-litigating a term already agreed elsewhere.

**The redline (validated ok:true).** Grant runs to "Customer, its affiliates and contractors acting on Customer's behalf"; "revocable" becomes "revocable only upon termination of this Agreement in accordance with paragraph 4"; "non-transferable, non-assignable" becomes "non-assignable (except as permitted under the assignment provisions of this Agreement)."

One drafting note for your review: I referred to "the assignment provisions of this Agreement" rather than a specific number. The assignment text sits in a paragraph labelled "(h)" and I could not confirm from the flat preamble structure whether it is 9(h) or another number — worth pinning to the correct citation before the clause goes out.
